chunks: Muḥammad ibn Zayd al-Ṭabarī narrated to me. He said: A man from the merchants of Fārs, from among some of the mawālī of Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, wrote to him asking permission concerning the khums.
So he wrote to him: In the Name of Allah, the All-Merciful, the All-Compassionate.

Indeed Allah is All-Encompassing, Generous. He has guaranteed reward for deeds, and anxiety upon constriction. No wealth is halal except through a means that Allah has made halal. And indeed the khums is our support for our religion, for our dependants, for our mawālī, and for what we expend and purchase for the protection of our honor against those whose assault we fear.

So do not withhold it from us, and do not deprive yourselves of our du'a for as much as you are able. For paying it is the key to your sustenance, the purification of your sins, and what you send ahead for yourselves for the day of your need. And the Muslim is the one who fulfills for Allah what he has pledged to Him, and the Muslim is not one who answers with the tongue while opposing with the heart. And peace.

key_terms.الْخُمُسَ: khums; the one-fifth due designated as a religious financial obligation
key_terms.تَمْحِيصُ ذُنُوبِكُمْ: purification of your sins; cleansing and removal of sins
key_terms.دُعَاءَنَا: our supplication; the Imam’s prayer for the payer
key_terms.عَهِدَ: he pledged or covenanted; what one commits to before Allah
key_terms.عَوْنُنَا: our support; that by which the Ahl al-Bayt are assisted in their affairs
key_terms.فَاقَتِكُمْ: your time of need and poverty
key_terms.مَوَالِينَا: our loyal followers and affiliates in wilayah
key_terms.مِفْتَاحُ رِزْقِكُمْ: the key to your sustenance; a means to opening provision

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام say about the purpose and importance of paying khums?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the obligation and legitimacy of khums, presenting it as a lawful financial right tied to the support of the Imam’s religious mission, dependants, and loyal followers. It also frames paying khums as a source of barakah in sustenance, expiation of sins, and a sign of sincerity and faithfulness to one’s covenant with Allah.
